output.sql: SELECT p.method AS payment_method, COUNT(*) AS payment_count, ROUND(AVG(p.paid_at - o.order_date)::numeric, 2) AS avg_days_to_pay FROM marts.fct_payments p JOIN marts.fct_orders o ON o.order_id = p.order_id GROUP BY p.method ORDER BY avg_days_to_pay;
output.explanation: Days to pay is measured as the payment's paid_at date minus the order's order_date, joining fct_payments to fct_orders on order_id. Results are grouped by payment method, with the average rounded to 2 decimals and the number of payments included for context. No revenue filter is applied, since the question concerns all payments; if only revenue orders should count, add WHERE o.is_revenue. The query has not been executed.
